subject: Geopolitics
title: The Lithium Triangle
description: A quick, practical guide to The Lithium Triangle.

hook.text: Bolivia, Argentina, and Chile sit atop 60% of the world's lithium. Electric cars run on their salt flats.

buildup.text: Lithium powers batteries for EVs, phones, and grid storage. Demand is projected to increase 40x by 2040.

discovery.text: Whoever controls lithium supply chains shapes the electric future. It's the new oil in economic importance.

twist.text: Bolivia has the most lithium but can't extract it economically. Political instability scares investors away.

climax.text: China, the US, and Europe are all competing for lithium contracts across South America. The scramble is underway.

punchline.text: The fuel of the future sits under some of the poorest ground.

quiz.question: Why is the Lithium Triangle strategically important?
options: It contains 60% of world lithium reserves needed for batteries
It produces most of the world's solar panels
It controls key shipping lanes for mineral transport
